Subject: Data retention exception — post-call recap

Hi Camila / Rafael,

Thanks for the demo earlier — good conversation. Quick recap and our primary asks so we have alignment:

- Healthlytics is processing high-sensitivity patient identifiers and we need contractual and technical guarantees around retention and logging.
- Requirement 1: PII (names, SSNs, DOBs, etc.) must not be persisted in any logs or long-term storage. We need a 0-retention commitment for PII fields.
- Requirement 2: Application telemetry and non-PII metadata can be retained for operational debugging, but must be limited to 30 days and anonymized.
- Requirement 3: All processing for PHI/PII must be in eu-west-1.
- Requirement 4: We require an auditable attestation and ability to request proof (e.g., redaction logs, audit logs) on request.

Attached is our initial security/requirements checklist for reference. Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood can support a 0-retention exception for PII on a per-route basis in your hosted offering, or whether we need Dedicated/Private.
- If Hosted is possible, what controls and SLAs are required; if not, rough timeline and cost for Dedicated/Private.

Next steps from our side: I looped in security@healthlytics.com to be part of the technical thread. Would like a short proposal and recommended path by end of week.

Thanks,
Olivia Cheng
Head of Product / Health Data
Healthlytics

[Attachment: Healthlytics-security-requirements.pdf]

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear recap and for sharing the checklist. Great to meet you both today. Below is a concise summary of options and the path I recommend based on what we discussed.

TL;DR: We can support per-route retention controls, but the level of contractual assurance you need (0-retention + auditable attestation + EU-only processing) typically requires either:
1) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) for a full zero-retention guarantee and more granular audit controls; OR
2) Hosted with strict routing + redaction + short ephemeral logs, subject to an approved data-retention exception (legal review) and additional operational controls.

Options (high level):
- Hosted (preferred for speed):
  - We can implement per-route configurable retention. For PII fields we offer two approaches: an automated redaction pipeline (remove PII before persistence) or configurable 0-retention flag that prevents token-level logging.
  - Constraints: full 0-retention for PII in hosted mode requires an approved exception and additional monitoring/auditing steps. We can provide attestations but there are limits on live customer-controlled keying unless you move to Private.
  - Residency: we can pin processing to eu-west-1 for your routes, but will need entitlement in your account and a signed amendment.
- Dedicated / Private:
  - Provides stronger guarantees (no shared logs, KMS integration, private control plane). Best fit for strict 0-retention + auditability.
  - Timeline: ~3-6 weeks to provision & validate depending on capacity and security review.

What we need from Healthlytics to proceed:
- Data flow diagram showing where PII enters your system and which endpoints touch it (link or attachment).
- Exact acceptance criteria for what counts as PII vs non-PII for this scope.
- Which routes/API keys should be marked 0-retention.

I've attached a short one-pager showing our standard retention options and what would be locked behind a legal exception.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the data flow diagram + security checklist answers.
2) We loop in our Legal (Marissa) and Security/SE (Rafael) to draft an exception and a technical approach.
3) We produce a short MAP and timeline (target: 2-3 weeks for hosted exception; 3-6 for Dedicated).

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-min deep-dive next week with Rafael to review redaction and the technical controls.

Best,
Camila Reyes

camila.reyes@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Thanks for the context, Camila. High-level legal position and next steps below.

Legal conditions for approving a 0-retention exception (initial):
1) Exception must be scoped to specific API routes (route IDs to be provided by customer). No blanket platform-level zero-retention.
2) Customer must sign a DPA amendment that explicitly describes retention behavior, audit rights, and deletion SLAs.
3) Attestation: Redwood to provide an operational attestation (signed) and a technical runbook describing how deletion is enforced.
4) Audit rights: Limited to periodic attestations and ad-hoc evidence requests (we'll propose a process and redaction of sensitive internal logs).
5) Residual metadata: We will permit anonymized operational metadata for debugging but must be scoped (default 30 days).

Practical notes:
- Hosted is acceptable if SE can demonstrate redaction/0-logging for the named routes and Security signs off. If not comfortable, Dedicated/Private remains the fallback.
- We should avoid promises of irrevocable deletion without assessable proof mechanism. The attestation will be our contractual commitment while we work on supporting tooling for on-demand attestations.

Timeline: I can draft an amendment template (based on our standard exception-template) and propose language by EOD Thursday. We'll need Rafael's technical description to make the amendment precise.

Next steps for sales:
- Rafael: provide technical approach + demo plan by Wednesday.
- Camila: request route IDs and the data flow diagram from the customer (target Wed).
- Legal will prepare the amendment and circulate for internal review (target Dec 8 to send to customer).

Attaching the exception template I will use as a starting point. I'll redline once we have Rafael's text.
